Both teams require use of the same paper tray installing machine and this machine can make at most 23 printers of either type each day. Color printers generate a profit of $300 per printer while black and white printers generate a profit of $50 per printer. How many of each printer should be made to maximize the company's profit?

An accounting firm has senior accountants earning $4000 per week and junior accountants earning $2000 per week. The contracts with companies to provide accounting services require at least 80 accountants, of whom at least 7 must be senior accountants. To make sure there is enough experience on the accounting team, the number of senior accountants should be at least a third of the number to junior accountants. document: Ben is growing apples and pears on his orchard. He has 40 acres available on which he must grow a minimum of 6 acres of apples and a minimum of 20 acres of pears to meet demands. The profit per apple is $3 and the profit per pear is $8. He prefers to grow more pears than apples but limitations in his workforce allow him to grow at most twice the amount of pears as apples. How many of each fruit should Ben grow in order to maximize his profit? What is that profit?

A lighting company makes desk-lamps and night-lamps. There is an expected demand of at least 20 desk-lamps and 60 night-lamps each day. However, due to the size of their factory, they can make at most 84 desk-lamps and 320 night-lamps per day. To satisfy a contract, a minimum of 200 lamps must be made each day. If the profit per desk-lamp sold is $8 and the profit per night-lamp sold is $7, how many lamps of each type should be made to maximize profit?

Mr. Roberts want to invest in the telecom and healthcare industries. He has $200000 to invest. He has decided that the amount invested in telecom be at least three times as much as the amount invested in healthcare. But the money invested in telecom must be at most $40000. If investments in telecom earn 2% and investments in healthcare earn 1%, how much should Mr. Roberts invest in each to maximize profit?

A farmer has 170 hectares available to grow tomatoes and potatoes. She prefers to plant more tomatoes than potatoes, but the soil and weather conditions allow her to grow at most twice the amount of tomatoes to that of potatoes. In addition, she must grow at least 10 hectares of tomatoes and at least 50 hectares of potatoes to meet community demands. If the profit per hectare of tomatoes is $270 and the profit per hectare of potatoes is $400, how many hectares of each crop should she plant to maximize profit? What is this profit?

A audio company make two types of headphones: wired headphones and wireless headphones. Two different teams make each type of headphones. The wired team can make at most 50 wired headphones per day and the wireless team can make at most 110 wireless headphones per day. Both teams require use of a shared audio testing machine, and this machine can be used to make a maximum of 81 headphones per day. The profit per wired headphone is $80 and the profit per wireless headphone $10. How many of each headphone should be made to maximize profit?

Jacob has $4000 to invest. He has decided to invest in his favorite clothing company and his favorite tech company. He has decided that the money invested in his favorite clothing company must be at least four times as much as the amount invested in his favorite tech company. He has also limited himself to invest at most $800 in his favorite tech company. If the money invested in his favorite clothing company earns 9% and the money invested in his favorite tech company earns 8%, how much should he invest in each to maximize his profit?

He also estimates that at least 200 carrots but at most 700 carrots are sold each month. How many of each, carrots and cucumbers, should be sold in order to maximize the profit?

A farmer wants to manufacture a special plant nutrition using fertilizers A and B. Each kg of fertilizer A contains 14 units of nitrogen, 3 units of phosphoric acid, 4 units of vitamin A and 3 units of vitamin D. Each kg of fertilizer B contains 5 units of nitrogen, 10 units of phosphoric acid, 4 units of vitamin A and 8 units of vitamin D. To be effective, the plant nutrition requires a minimum 140 units of nitrogen, a minimum of 200 units of phosphoric acid, and no more than 580 units of vitamin A. How many kg of each fertilizer should be used to minimize the amount of vitamin D in the nutrition? What is the minimum amount of vitamin D?

Mrs. Watson wants to invest in the real-estate market and has a total budget of at most $1000000. She has two choices which include condos and detached houses. Each dollar invested in condos yields a $0.90 profit and each dollar invested in detached houses yields a $1 profit. A minimum of 10% of all money invested must be in condos, and at least $40000 must be in detached houses. document: A bakery uses a stand-mixer and a slow bake oven to make bread and cookies. Each machine can run for at most 2000 hours per year. To bake a loaf of bread takes 1 hour in the stand mixer and 2 hours in the oven. A batch of cookies requires 0.6 hours in the mixer and 1 hour in the oven. The profit per loaf of bread is $3 and the profit per batch of cookies is $2. How should the bakery operate to maximize total profit?

A glass factory makes two types of glass panes: a regular glass pane and a tempered glass pane. Both require time on a heating and cooling machine. Both machines are available for a maximum of 200 minutes per day. It takes 2 minutes in the heating machine and 4 minutes in the cooling machine to make one regular glass pane. It takes 4 minutes in the heating machine and 10 minutes in the cooling machine to make one tempered glass pane. The profit per pane of regular glass is $10 and the profit per pane of tempered glass is $8. How many panes of each glass type should the factory make to maximize profit? What is the maximum profit?

A souvenir shop makes wooden elephants and tigers with plastic ornaments. Each elephant requires 40 grams of wood and 10 grams of plastic. Each tiger requires 50 grams of wood and 20 grams of plastic. In a week, 6000 grams of wood and 5000 grams of plastic are available. The profit per elephant sold is $7 and the profit per tiger sold is $3. How many of each should be made in order to maximize profit?

An art store makes large and small art pieces. The store has available 200 units of paint, 60 units of glitter, and 100 units of glue. To make a large art piece requires 5 units of paint, 2 units of glitter, and 6 units of glue. To make a small art piece requires 3 units of paint, 1 unit of glitter, and 3 units of glue. The store must make at least 6 units of each large and small art pieces. If the profit per large art piece is $20 and the profit per small art piece is $16, how many of each should be made to maximize profit?

My family has decided to invest in real state for the first time. Currently, they have $1,000,000 to invest, some in apartments and the rest in townhouses. The money invested in apartments must not be greater than $300,000. They have decided that the money invested in apartments must be at least a half as much as that in townhouses.  If the apartments earn 7%, and the townhouses earn 18%, how much money should they invest in each to maximize profit?

document: My grandma is required to take two medicines Z1 and D3 everyday. She needs to take at least 4 grams of Z1 and 8 grams of D3 everyday. These medicines are available in two pills named Zodiac and Sunny. One pill of Zodiac contains 0.7 grams of Z1 while one pill of Sunny contains 1.6 grams of Z1. On the other hand, one pill of Zodiac contains 2.5 grams of D3 and one pill of Sunny contains 4 grams of D3. The cost per pill of Zodiac is $1 and the cost per pill of Sunny is $5. Formulate a LP such that the medicine requirement can be fulfilled at the lowest cost.

A hobbyist makes model trains and planes using wood and paint. A model train requires 2 units of wood and 2 units of paint. A model plane requires 5 units of wood and 4 units of paint. The hobbyist has available 84 units of wood and 70 units of paint. If the profit per model train is $6 and the profit per model plane is $7, how many of each should be made to maximize his profit?

An electronics store wants to optimize how many phones and laptops are enough to keep in inventory. A phone will earn the store $150 in profits, and a laptop will earn $70. A phone requires 1 sq ft of floor space, whereas a laptop requires 5 sq ft. In total, 600 sq ft of floor space is available. The store stocks only phones and laptops. Corporate has required that at least 60% of all appliances in stock be laptops. Finally, a phone costs $600 for the store, and a laptop, $200. The store wants to spend at most $3000. Formulate an LP that can be used to maximize the store's profit.

A candy store mixes regular candy and sour candy to prepare two products, regular mix and sour surprise mix. Each kilogram of the regular mix contains 0.5 kg of regular candy and 0.3 kg of sour candy. The profit per kilogram of the regular mix is $2. Each kilogram of the sour surprise mix contains 0.2 kg of regular candy and 0.6 kg of sour candy. The profit per kilogram of the sour surprise mix is $3. The candy store has 50 kg of regular candy and 40 kg of sour candy available. How many kilograms of each type of candy mix should be created to maximize profits?

A suspicious factory has 60 sq. feet of space. It makes bootleg phones and laptops. Phones require 3 hours of labor and cost $15 for each sq. foot of space allocated for phone production (cost of electricity and equipment). Laptops require 6 hours of labor and cost $9 for each sq. foot of space allocated for laptop production. Phones produce a net revenue of $30 per sq. foot while laptops produce a net revenue of $50 per sq. foot. The factory wants to spend at most $7000 and 3000 hours of labor. What is the optimal factory layout to maximize revenue?

A electronics store sells premium desktops with more power as well as regular desktops for everyday use. Each premium desktop costs the store $1000 to make and yields a profit of $900. Each regular desktop costs the store $700 to make and yields a profit of $200. The store sells at most 400 desktops each month and wants to spend at most $500000 on making the desktops. How many of each should be made and sold to maximize profit?

A car manufacturer makes two versions of the same car, a regular model and a premium model. They make x1 regular models per day and x2 premium models per day. The profit per regular model is $3000 and the profit per premium model is $16000 (x1 and x2 are unknown values both greater than or equal to 0). The daily demand for these cars is limited to and most 10 regular models and 4 premium models. In addition, the manufacturer can make a maximum of 11 cars of either type per day. How many cars of each model should the manufacturer make in order to maximize profit?

You are designing an office space with two types of desks: long desks and short desks. You can spend at most $3000. Long desks cost $200, take up 20 square feet of space, and seat 10 employees. Short desks cost $60, take up 2 square feet of space, and seat 3 employees. The office can have at most 100 square feet of desks. How many of each desk should you buy in order to maximize the seating availability?

Ayse produces a plant growth compound by mixing two types of fertilizer: C and Y. This growth compound must contain at least 6 units of nitrous oxide and 7 units of vitamin mix. Fertilizer C and Y cost $3 and $2 per kg respectively. Fertilizer C contains 2.1 units of nitrous oxide per kg and 2 units of vitamin mix per kg. Fertilizer Y contains 6 units of nitrous oxide per kg and 1 unit of vitamin mix per kg. Determine the minimum cost of Ayse's compound.

Sleep inducing medicine and anti-inflammatory medicine is found in two pills, pill A and pill B. One pill A contains 4 units of sleep inducing medicine and 7 units of anti-inflammatory medicine. One pill B contains 10 units of sleep-inducing medicine and 1 unit of anti-inflammatory medicine. The cost per pill for pill A is $8 and the cost per pill for pill B is $7. A patient must consume these two pills to get at least 30 units of sleep-inducing medicine and 40 units of anti-inflammatory medicine. Formulate a LP to minimize the cost for the patient.

document: A car manufacturer makes two types of car oils: Oil Max and Oil Max Pro. A container of Oil Max contains 57 grams of substance A, 42 grams of substance B and 30 grams of substance C. A container of Oil Max Pro contains 21 grams of substance A, 7 grams of substance B and 36 grams of substance C. The car manufacturer has 726 grams of substance A, 351 grams of substance B, 1545 grams of substance C. In addition, the profit per container of Oil Max is $8 and the profit per container of Oil Max Pro is $14. How many containers of each of oil should the car manufacturer make to maximize profit?

A food truck owner can spend at most $10000 on mangos and guavas. A mango costs the food truck owner $4 and a guava costs him $2. Spices are added and each mango is sold for a profit of $2 while each guava is sold for a profit of $6. The owner estimates that at least 80 mangos but at the most 87 are sold each month. He also estimates that the number of guavas sold is at most a third of the mangos sold. How many mangos and guavas should be sold in order to maximize the profit?

An ice cream store makes chocolate and vanilla ice cream by the gallon. In a week, they must make at least 3 gallons of each type but at most 6 gallons of chocolate ice cream and at most 7 gallons of vanilla ice cream. It takes 1 hour to produce a gallon of chocolate ice cream and 4 hours to produce a gallon of vanilla ice cream. In a week, 40 hours are available to make ice cream. In addition at least 9 workers are needed with 1 working on the chocolate ice cream and 4 on the vanilla ice cream at any time. If the profit per gallon of chocolate ice cream is $100 and the profit per gallon of vanilla ice cream is $500, how many gallons of each should be made to maximize profit?

Mark has 70 acres of land available to grow potatoes and cucumbers that he sells at a farmers' market. He must grow at least 16 acres of potatoes and 25 acres of cucumbers to meet his contract. Mark prefers to grow more cucumbers than potatoes, but he only has enough resources to grow at most twice the amount of cucumbers as potatoes. If the profit per acre of potatoes is $300 and the profit per acre of cucumbers is $690, how many acres of each should he grow to maximize his profit? What is that profit?

A flooring company produces engineered hardwood and vinyl planks. Their sales forecasts show an expected demand of at least 30,000 square foot of hardwood and 9,000 square feet of vinyl planks each week. To satisfy a shipping contract, a total of at least 40,000 square feet of flooring much be shipped each week. Due to a labor shortage issue, no more than 60,000 square feet of hardwood and 20,000  square feet of vinyl  can be produced weekly. If a square foot of hardwood flooring yields a profit of $1.5 and a square foot of vinyl planks produces a $2 profit, how many of each type of flooring should be made weekly to maximize the company's profit?

A berry farmer has two farms, an old and new farm, where he grows raspberries, blueberries, and strawberries. He has a contract to provide a local store with 8 kg of raspberries, 7 kg of blueberries, and 14 kg of strawberries. At his old farm, it cost $200 to operate per day and he can harvest and deliver 3 kg of raspberries, 3 kg of blueberries, and 6 kg of strawberries in a day. At his new farm, it costs $100 to operate per day and he can harvest and deliver 6 kg of raspberries, 1 kg of blueberries, and 3 kg of strawberries in a day. Formulate a LP to meet his contract while minimizing his cost.

Jordan is a chef. He wants to design a diet consisting of Kebabs and Rice.  Assume that each serving of Rice costs $2 and contains 200 calories and 3.1 grams of protein. Assume that each serving of Kebab costs $3 and contains 300 calories and 6 grams of protein. He's interested in spending as little money as possible but he wants to ensure that his meals have at least 1800 calories and at least 20 grams of protein per day. Formulate a linear programming problem that will help minimize the cost of the diet.

A company sells custom scooters and bikes for customers. The profit per scooter is $300 and the profit per bike is $200. Each product requires time with the design team and engineering team. Each scooter needs 3 hours with the design team and 4 hours with the engineering team. Each bike needs 6 hours with the design team and 9 hours with the engineering team. Per month, there are 3000 hours available on the design team and 5000 hours available on the engineering team. How many of each should the company make per month to maximize profit?

John has a 500 acre berry farm on which to plant blueberries and raspberries. John has $20000 to spend on watering and 457 days worth of labor available. For each acre of blueberries, 9 days worth of labor and $14 in watering costs is required. For each acre of raspberries, 4 days worth of labor and $15 in watering costs is required. The profit per acre of blueberries is $45 and the profit per acre of raspberries is $140. Formulate an LP problem in order to maximize profit.

A man  only eats vegetable and fruits. A serving of vegetables contains 3 units of vitamins and 4 units of minerals. A serving of fruit contains 6 units of vitamins and 1 unit of minerals. He wants to eat at least 30 units of vitamins and 40 units of minerals. If vegetables cost $4 per serving and fruits cost $8 per serving, how many servings of each should he eat to minimize his cost?

A bakery bakes bagels and croissants. A batch of bagels can be made using 3 hours of oven time and 0.13 hours of pastry chef time. A batch of croissants is more complicated, so while they take 1 hour of oven time, they take 3 hours of pastry chef time. In a day, the bakery has at most 60 hours available for the oven and 42 pastry chef hours available. Using all the available capacity, what is the maximum profit the bakery can generate assuming the profit per batch is $40 and $70 respectively for a batch of bagels and a batch of croissants.

Running factory 2 for 1 hour costs $700 and produces 7 black teddy bears and 7 white teddy bears. (but no brown ones). document: A farmer has 400 acres of land to grow turnips and pumpkins. Turnips require 90 minutes of watering and $100 worth of pesticide per acre. Pumpkins require 50 minutes of watering and $90 worth of pesticide per acre. The farmer has 30000 minutes available for watering and $41000 available to spend on pesticide. If the revenue per acre of turnips is $200 and the revenue per acre of pumpkins is $620, how many acres of each should he grow to maximize his revenue.

A school employs staff and substitute teachers. Per shift, staff teachers work 8 hours and get paid $200. Per shift, substitute teachers work 2 hours and get paid $60. For the summer term, the school requires 500 hours of teaching availability. If the school has a budget of $30000, how many of each teacher should be hired to minimize the total number of teachers?

A gem factory has two drills, a high intensity one and a low intensity one. Each day, the high intensity drill can process 40 gems and requires 40 units of water to dissipate heat. Each day, the low intensity drill can process 20 gems and requires 30 units of water to dissipate heat. Each day the factory must process 400 gems and they have available 1000 units of water. Since the high intensity drill produces a lot of noise pollution, at most 20% of the drills can be high intensity ones. Further, at least 8 should be low intensity drills. How many of each drill should be used to minimize the total number of drills needed?

A sandwich company can open two types of stores, a dine-in place and a food-truck. A dine-in place can make 200 sandwiches per day and requires 10 employees to operate. A food-truck can make 30 sandwiches per day and requires 5 employees to operate. The company must make at least 300 sandwiches per day but they only have available 52 employees. How many of each type of store should the company open to minimize the total number of stores?

There are two processes, process A and process B, to plate a coin with gold. Process A requires 2 units of gold, 3 wires, and can plate 7 coins. Process B requires 7 units of gold, 2 wires, and can plate 4 coins. There are 300 units of gold and 500 wires available. How many processes of each type should be run to maximize the total number of coins that can be plated?

A woodshop can purchase two types of saws, a miter saw and a circular saw. A miter saw can cut 30 planks of wood and produces 50 units of sawdust per day. A circular saw can cut 90 planks of wood and produces 80 units of sawdust per day. The woodshop must cut at least 1300 planks of wood per day. However, to avoid too much pollution in the woodshop they can produce at most 4000 units of sawdust per day. How many of each type of saw should be purchased to minimize the total number of saws needed?

A farmer has 300 acres of land on which he must process hay using either a windrower or hay harvester. For each acre of land, the windrower can process 6 kg of hay while the hay harvester can process 5 kg of hay. Per acre, the windrower produces 8 kg of methane gas and requires 3 kg of fuel. On the other hand, the hay harvester produces 2 kg of methane gas per acre and requires 1 kg of fuel. There are 200 kg of fuel available and the farmer can produce at most 1000 kg of methane gas. For how many acres should each machine be used to maximize the amount of hay processed?

A new fast food place makes wraps and platters. Each wrap requires 3 units of meat and 2 units of rice. Each platter requires 8 units of meant and 3 units of rice. While each wrap takes 9 minutes to make, each platter takes 4 minutes to make. The fast food place must use at least 2000 units of meat and 3200 units of rice. Since wraps are easier to eat on the go, at least 2 times as many wraps need to be made as platter. How many of each should the fast food place make to minimize the total production time?

An amusement park is installing ticket machines, both cash-based and card-only machines. A cash-based machine can process 30 people per hour while a card-only machine can process 20 people per hour. The cash-based machine needs 3 rolls of paper per hour while the card-only machine requires 10 rolls of paper per hour. The amusement park needs to be able to process at least 900 people per hour but can use at most 100 rolls of paper per hour. Since most people prefer to pay by cash, the number of card-only machines must not exceed the number of cash-based machines. How many of each machine should be bought to minimize the total number of machines in the park?

A honey farmer sells his honey in glass and plastic jars. A glass jar can hold 210 ml of honey while a plastic jar can hold 200 ml of honey. Since glass jars are more expensive, at least twice as many plastic jars must be filled as glass jars. However, at least 10 glass jars should be filled. If the farmer has 40000 ml of honey, how many jars of each should be filled to maximize the total number of bottles filled?

A city employs seasonal and permanent snow removers. A seasonal snow remover works 9 hours per shift and gets paid $70. A permanent snow remover works 5 hours per shift and gets paid $130. Currently the city needs 200 hours of snow remover labor after a heavy snowfall. If the city has a budget of $10000, how many of each type of worker should be hired to minimize the total number of snow removers?

A cell phone company is building rural and urban factories. A rural factory can make 200 phones per day and requires 10 managers. An urban factory can make 100 phones per day and requires 30 managers. The company has available 400 managers and must make at least 6000 phones per day. How many of each factory type should be built to minimize the total number of factories?

An ice cream store can buy two machines, a counter-top sized one and a fridge sized one, to make ice cream. The counter-top sized one can produce 40 cones worth of ice cream every day while the fridge sizes one can produce 160 cones worth of ice cream every day. The counter-top sized machine outputs 30 units of heat while the fridge sized one outputs 50 units of heat. The ice cream store can output at most 600 units of heat per day and must produce at least 700 cones worth of ice cream. How many of each machine should they buy to minimize the total number of machines needed?

There are two specialized containers, a small and large one, that are used to make a pharmaceutical paste. The small container requires 8 units of water and 9 units of the powdered pill to make 40 units of the paste. The large container requires 40 units of water and 40 units of the powdered pill to make 20 units of the paste. The pharmacy has available 400 units of water and 1000 units of the powdered pill. How many of each container should be used to maximize the amount of paste that can be made?

An oil and gas company operates on 500 acres of land where they use oil wells of small and large size. Per acre of land, a small oil well can produce 3 barrels of oil. Per acre of land, a large oil well can produce 7 barrels of oil. However, a small oil well produces 6 units of pollution and requires 7 drill bits per acre and a large oil well produces 10 units of pollution and requires 6 drill bits per acre. The company has available 4100 drill bits and due to strict environmental laws can produce at most 2900 units of pollution. For how many acres should each oil well be used to maximize the total production of oil?

A burger chain is buying both gas and electric grills to make burger patties. A gas grill can cook 40 patties per minute while an electric grill can cook 20 patties per minute. The gas grill requires 40 units of cooking oil per minute while the electric grill requires 45 units of cooking oil per minute. Since the gas grill patties taste better, the number of electric grills must be less than the number of gas grills. Further, the burger chain wants to be able to make at least 120 patties per minute and use at most 150 units of cooking oil per minute. How many of each grill should be bought to minimize the total number of grills in the store?

If the firm has a budget of $10000, how many of each healthcare worker should be scheduled to minimize the total number of workers?

A laundromat can buy two types of washing machines, a top-loading model and a front-loading model. The top-loading model can wash 30 items per day while the front-loading model can wash 140 items per day. The top-loading model consumes 120 kWh per day while the front-loading model consumes 80 kWh per day. The laundromat must be able to wash at least 4000 items per day and has available 10000 kWh per day. Since the top-loading machine are harder to use, at most 50% of the machines can be top-loading. document: A bee farmer transports his honey in small and large bottles. A small bottle can take 6 units of honey while a large bottle can take 30 units of honey. Finally, he can transport at most 400 bottles total and at least 80 must be large bottles. How many of each bottle should be use to maximize the total amount of honey he can transport?

An international goods exporter uses ships and planes to transport goods. A ship can take 70 containers worth of goods and uses 800 liters of fuel per trip. A plane can take 30 containers worth of goods and uses 400 liters of fuel per trip. The company needs to transport at least 800 containers worth of goods. In addition, there can be at most 20 plane trips made and a minimum of 70% of the trips made must be by ship. How many of each trip should be made to minimize the total amount of fuel consumed?

There has been an oil spill in the ocean and ducks need to be taken to shore to be cleaned either by boat or by canoe. A boat can take 7 ducks per trip while a canoe can take 5 ducks per trip. Since the boats are motor powered, they take 30 minutes per trip while the canoes take 50 minutes per trip. In order to avoid further environmental damage, there can be at most 9 boat trips and at least 40% of the trips should be by canoe. If at least 200 ducks need to be taken to shore, how many of each transportation method should be used to minimize the total amount of time needed to transport the ducks?

A soda company sends bottles of their soda to stores around the city in old and new vans. An old van can take 80 soda bottles while a new van can take 100 soda bottles. An old van produces 30 units of pollution while a new van only produces 20 units of pollution. The company needs to send at least 4000 bottles. In addition, at most 20 new vans can be used. How many of each van should be used to minimize the total amount of pollution produced?

A lawn mowing service provides neighborhood services using small teams and large teams. A small team requires 2 employees and can mow 80 sq ft of lawn. A large team requires 3 employees and can mow 70 sq ft of lawn. The company has 100 employees available. Because most people have smaller lawns in the city, the number of small teams must be at least 2 times as much as the number of large teams. In addition, to make sure the company can meet all demands, there has to be at least 10 large teams and at least 6 small teams. How many of each team type should be used to maximize the amount of lawn that can be mowed?

An aquarium does shows using otters and dolphins. An otter will do 2 tricks at a time and requires 2 treats to do so. A dolphin will do 1 trick at a time and requires 9 treats to do so. Since dolphins are more popular, at least 7 dolphins must be used and at most 40% of the performers can be otters. If the aquarium only has 400 treats available, maximize the total number of tricks that can be preformed.

A shoe company supplies shoes to stores via vans and trucks. A van can transport 70 pairs of shoes while a truck can transport 200 pairs of shoes. The company must supply a minimum of 3000 pairs of shoes around the city. Since most stores are small, the number of trucks used cannot exceed the number of vans used.  Find the minimum number of vans that can be used?

An oil and gas company is sending their oil to the port using containers and trucks. A container can hold 20 units of oil while a truck can hold 60 units of oil. Due to government restrictions, the number of trucks used has to at most half the number of containers used. If at least 3000 units of oil need to be sent to the port and at least 13 containers need to be used, minimize the total number of containers and trucks needed.

A school is organizing a field trip to a science center and wants to hire small buses and large buses. A small bus can carry 10 students while a large bus can carry 60 students.  The school needs to provide transportation for at least 700 students.  In addition, since the parking lot is rather small, a maximum of 30% of the buses can be large buses. How many of each type of bus should be hired to minimize the total number of buses?

A meat shop ships their burger patties using refrigerated trucks and vans. Each truck can take 600 patties at a cost of $200 per trip. Each van can take 700 patties at a cost of $50 per trip. Because the trucks have difficulty moving around in the city, the number of trucks must not exceed the number of vans. The meat shop has to ship at least 70000 patties and they have a budget of $13100. How should they plan their shipment to minimize the total number of trips?

A florist transports his flowers to stores in small bouquets and large bouquets. A small bouquet has 4 flowers while a large bouquet has 5 flowers. The florist can transport at most 60 small bouquets and 40 large bouquets. In total, he can transport at most 50 bouquets and he must transport at least 10 large bouquets. Since small bouquets are more popular, he must transport at least twice as many small bouquets as large bouquets. How many of each bouquet should he transport to maximize the total number of flowers that reach the stores?

A toy store decides to deliver gifts using two shipping companies, a new one and an old one. The new company can deliver 80 gifts per trip while the old company can deliver 50 gifts per trip. The new company uses 20 liters of diesel per trip while the old company uses 70 liters of diesel per trip. The toy store needs to deliver at least 600 gifts. There can be at most 10 trips made by the new company. In order to make sure that the old company does not go out of business, at least 60% of all trips must be made by the old company. How many trips should each company make to minimize the total amount of diesel used?

A zoo needs to transport their monkeys to the vet either by bus or by car. A bus can transport 30 monkeys per trip and takes 50 minutes. A car can transport 9 monkeys per trip and takes 10 minutes. There can be at most 5 bus trips. In addition, since the monkeys get aggressive when there are too many in one place at least 50% of the trips should be by car. If the zoo needs to transport 200 monkeys, how many trips of each should be done to minimize the total time required to transport the monkeys?

A farmer decides to move his cows to a nearby farm using helicopters and trucks. A helicopter can take 4 cows per trip and creates 3 units of pollution. A truck can take 5 cows per trip and creates 20 units of pollution. The farmer needs to transport 100 cows and he only has enough money for at most 10 truck trips. How many of each type of trip should be taken to minimize the total amount of pollution produced?

A sand company delivers sand for playgrounds in small and large containers. A small container requires 1 person to unload and can hold 30 units of sand. A large container requires 5 people to unload and can hold 40 units of sand. Since most playgrounds are small, the number of small containers used must be thrice the number of large containers used. In addition, there must be at least 9 small containers and 5 large containers used. If the company has 200 people available, maximize the amount of sand that they can deliver.

A meal service company delivers meals to customers either on electric bikes or scooters. A bike can hold 7 meals and requires 2 units of charge. A scooter can hold 9 meals and requires 3 units of charge. Since the city is more friendly towards scooters, at most 20% of the electric vehicles can be bikes and at least 30 scooters must be used. If the company only has 300 units of charge available, how many of each vehicle should be used to maximize the number of meals that can be delivered?

Since large planes cause more pollution, the number of large planes must be less than the number of small planes. If the manufacturer wants to deliver at least 400 cars, find the minimum number of planes that can be used.

document: A mine sends ore to the surface in small and large wagons. A small wagon hold 10 units of ore while a large wagon holds 60 units of ore. To avoid taking up too much space on the ramps, the number of small wagons must be at least twice as much as the number or large wagons. In addition, at least 6 large wagons must be used. If 1000 units of ore need to taken to the surface, minimize the total number of wagons needed.

A theme park transports its visitors around the park either by scooter or rickshaw. A scooter can carry 4 people while a rickshaw can carry 2 people. To avoid excessive pollution, at most 50% of the vehicles used can be rickshaws. If the park needs to transport at least 600 visitors, minimize the total number of scooters used.

A company in the middle east delivers their packages to customers on camels and horses. A camel can carry 30 packages while a horse can carry 100 packages. A camel requires 10 units of food while a horse requires 20 units of food. The company needs to deliver at least 800 packages and they have 280 units of food available. Since horses are not as suited for the hot climate, the number of horses cannot exceed the number of camels. How many of each animal should be used to minimize the total number of animals?

A snack exporter sends snacks to his customer in small and large suitcases. A small suitcase can hold 30 snacks while a large suitcase can hold 70 snacks. Most customer prefer small suitcases, and so at least twice as many small suitcases must be used as large suitcases. The exporter has available at most 40 small suitcases and 30 large suitcases. If he must send at least 13 large suitcases and can send  at most 40 suitcases in total, how many of each should he send to maximize the total number of snacks that can be delivered?

A mail delivery service in an island village delivers mail by regular and speed boats. A regular boat can carry 30 pieces of mail per trip and uses 20 liters of gas. A speed boat can carry 60 pieces of mail per trip and uses 30 liters of gas. There can be at most 30 regular boat trips. Since customers want their mail as fast as possible, at least 60% of the trips must be made by speed boats. If the service needs to deliver 600 pieces of mail, how many trips of each should be made to minimize the total amount of gas consumed?

A chicken farmer has sold his chicken and they need to be transported either by bus or by car. A bus can take 50 chicken and takes 3 hours per trip. A car can take 80 chicken and takes 3.0 hours per trip. There can be at most 20 bus trips and at least 50% of the trips must be by car. If the farmer needs to transport 1500 chicken, how many trips of each should be done to minimize the total time needed to transport the chicken?

Children can go to school either by van or by minibus. A van can take 4 kids and produces 8 units of pollution. A minibus can take 9 kids and produced 9 units of pollution. There are at least 120 kids than need to go to school and at most 9 minibuses can be used. In addition, the number of vans used must exceed the number of minibuses. How many of each should be used to minimize the total amount of pollution produced?

document: A toy store hires seasonal and full-time volunteers to deliver gifts and gives them points for service. A seasonal volunteer can deliver 8 gifts and gets 3 points. A full-time volunteer can deliver 4 gifts and gets 8 points. The store can only give out 300 points. In addition, a maximum of 20% of the volunteers can be seasonal and at least 9 must be full-time. How many of each volunteer is needed to maximize the total number of gifts that can be delivered?

A jam company sends its product out in small and large jars. A small jar can hold 40 ml of jam while a large jar can hold 100 ml of jam. Most store prefer the smaller size and so the number of large jars cannot exceed the number of small jars. If the company wants to ship at least 70000 ml of jam, find the minimum number of jars that can be used.

A corn farmer sends his corn to the city by either tractor or car.  A tractor can carry 50 kg of corn while a car can carry 30 kg of corn. Since tractors are very slow, the number of cars used has to be at least twice the number of tractors used. If at least 700 kg of corn need to be sent to the city, minimize the total number of tractors and cars needed.

A village hosts a banquet and provides bike and car transportation for everyone. A bike can take 5 people while a car can take 9 people. Since cars are more expensive, at most 60% of the vehicles can be cars. If the village needs to transport at least 300 people, how many of each vehicle should be used to minimize the total number of bikes needed?

An industrial tire company delivers large tires for equipment to remote engineering sites either by cargo planes or ultrawide trucks. Each cargo plane can transport 20 tires per trip and costs $500. Each ultrawide truck can transport 7 tires per trip and costs $600. The company needs to transport at least 100 tires and has available $11000. Because most remote sites don't have proper airports, the number of plane trips cannot exceed the number of ultrawide truck trips. How many trips of each should be done to minimize the total number of trips?

A water salesman collects water from a glacier and transports it in either small or large kegs. A small keg can hold 60 liters of water while a large keg can hold 90 liters of water. The salesman has available at most 20 small kegs and 7 large kegs. Since small kegs are easier to carry, at least twice as may small kegs must be used than large kegs. If he can transport at most 14 kegs total and at least 4 kegs must be large, how many of each should he use to maximize the total amount of glacial water he can transport?

A tropical city full of islands sends mail either by submarine or by boat. A submarine can carry 80 pieces of mail per trip and uses 20 liters of gas. A boat can carry 70 pieces of mail per trip and uses 13 liters of gas. There can be at most 4 submarine trips and a minimum of 90% of the trips must be by boat. If the city needs to transport at least 600 pieces of mail, how many of each transportation should they use to minimize the total amount of gas used?

The weather is freezing and the fish in the pond need to be transported either by helicopter or car. A helicopter can take 20 fish per trip and takes 50 minutes. A car can take 40 fish per trip and takes 20 minutes. Since helicopter trips are expensive, there can be at most 6 helicopter trips. In addition, at least 80% of the trips should be by car. If at least 500 fish need to transported, how many of each trip should be taken to minimize the total time needed?

A tourist spot in the mountains allows visitors to travel to the top either by hot-air balloon or gondola lift. A hot air balloon can carry 3 visitors while a gondola lift can carry 4 visitors. Each hot air balloon produces 20 units of pollution while each gondola lift produces 13 units of pollution. There can be at most 20 hot-air balloon rides and at least 100 visitors need to be transported. How many of each type of transport method should be taken to minimize the total pollution produced?

A factory transports rice to the city in horse-drawn carts that are either medium or large size. A medium sized cart requires 4 horses and can carry 20 kg of rice. A large sized cart requires 8 horses and can carry 40 kg of rice.  The factory has 100 horses available. Because the horses don't get along well, the number of medium sized carts must be three times the number of large sized carts. In addition, there must be at least 3 medium sized carts and at least 3 large sized carts. How many of each cart size should be used to maximize the amount of rice that can be transported?

A dog school trains labradors and golden retrievers to deliver newspaper. A labrador can deliver 10 newspapers at a time and requires 4 small bone treats for service. A golden retriever can deliver 20 newspapers at a time and requires 8 small bone treats per service. The school only has 1200 small bone treats available. In addition, at least 40 golden retrievers must be used and at most 90% of the dogs can be labradors. How many of each dog should be used to maximize the number of newspapers that can be delivered?

A construction company in the tropics uses cows and elephants to carry bricks. A cow can carry 10 bricks on its back while an elephant can carry 30 bricks on its back. To avoid having elephants create too much traffic, the number of elephant cannot exceed the number of cows. In addition, there can be at most twice the number of cows as elephants. If the company needs to transport at least 700 bricks, find the minimum number of animals, cows and elephants, that can be used..

A farmer on an island sends corn to the main land either by ferry or light rail. Each ferry trip can take 10 boxes of corn while each light rail trip can take 21 boxes of corn. Since ferry trips are slow, the number of light rail trip has to be at least 2 times the number of ferry trips. If the farmer wants to send at least 800 boxes of corn, minimize the total number of trips of either type needed.

A factory provides rides for its employees in either taxis or company cars. Each taxi ride can take 3 employees while each company car ride can take 4 employees. Since buying and maintaining cars is expensive, at most 40% of the rides can be company car rides. However, there has to be at least 20 company car rides. If the company needs to transport at least 400 employees, how many rides of each should be done to minimize the total number of taxi rides.

A grape farmer transports his grapes in either small crates or large crates. A small crate can take 300 grapes while a large crate can take 900.  Because his customers prefer smaller crates, at least 2 times as many small crates must be used than large crates. The farmer has available at most 50 small crates and at most 80 large crates. In addition, his truck can take at most 90 crates total and he must use at least 6 large crates. How many of each crate should he use to maximize the total number of grapes he can transport?

A shipping company need to transport packages by either truck or car. A truck can transport 100 packages per trip while a car can transport 20 packages per trip. In addition, a truck uses 30 liters of gas per trip while a car uses 18 liters of gas per trip. There can be at most 4 truck trips made and at least 20% of all the trips must be made by car. The company needs to transport at least 300 packages. How many of each transportation should they use to minimize the total amount of gas consumed?

There has been a horrible accident and patients need to be taken to the hospital by either a helicopter or bus. A helicopter can transport 3 patients per trip and takes 1 hour. On the other hand, a bus can transport 5 patients per trip and takes 4 hours. At least 150 patients need to be transported and at least 20% of the trips should be by helicopter. In addition, there can be at most 7 bus trips. How should the patients be taken to minimize the total time to transport the patients?

Employees have the option of car-pooling to work or taking the company bus. A car can take 3 employees and produces 6 units of pollution, while a bus can take 30 employees and produces 20 units of pollution. At least 600 employees need to be transported and at most 3 buses can be used. How many of each type of transport should be taken to minimize the total pollution produced.

A magic school sends letters to student either by carrier pigeons or owls. A carrier pigeon can carry two letters at a time and requires 4 treats for service. An owl can carry 6 letters at a time and requires 6 treats for service.  At most 30% of the birds can be owls. In addition, the school only has 700 treats available and at least 30 carrier pigeons must be uses. How many of each bird can be used to maximize the total number of letters that can be sent.

An international shipping company uses large and small ships to transport containers around the world. A large ship can carry 900 containers while a small ship can carry 400 containers. Because most ports are small, the number of large ships cannot exceed the number of small ships. If the company is under contract needs to transport at least 2000 containers, find the minimum number of ships that can be used.

A large fishing boat sends fish back to shore either by small canoes or smaller diesel boats. A canoe can carry back 8 fish while a small diesel boat can carry back 13 fish. In order to follow environmental rules, the number of small canoes used has to be at least 5 times as many as the number of diesel boats uses. If  at least 2000 fish need to be transported to shore, minimize the total number of canoes and diesel boats needed.

A volunteer organization transports voters to the polls on Election Day either by vans or cars. They have vans which can carry 8 people and cars which can carry 2 people.  They need to transport at least 400 voters to the polls. In addition, at most 60% of the vehicles can be vans. How many of each vehicle should be used to minimize the total number of cars used?

A car manufacturing company makes hamburgers and chicken wraps for workers. They need to ensure workers get at least 2700 calories, 30 grams of protein, and 60 grams of carbs. One hamburger costs $4.6 and contains 500 calories, 27 grams of protein, and 10 grams of carbs. One chicken wrap costs $3 and contains 830 calories, 6 grams of protein, and 8 grams of carbs. What is the minimum cost diet that the company can provide for its workers?

A meat processing plant uses two machines, a meat slicer and a meat packer, to make their hams and pork ribs. To produce one batch of hams requires 6 hours on the meat slicer and 3.5 hours on the meat packer. To produce one batch of pork ribs requires 4 hours on the meat slicer and 7.0 hours on the meat packer. Each machine runs for at most 6000 hours per year. If the profit per batch of hams is $240 and the profit per batch of pork ribs is $200, how many batches of each should be made to maximize profit?

An appliance company sells and installs refrigerators and stoves. Each refrigerator takes 100 minutes of mover time and 10 minutes of setup time. Each stove takes 85 minutes of mover time and 14 minutes of setup time. The company has available 40000 minutes of mover time and 16000 minutes of setup time. If the profit per refrigerator is $300 and the profit per stove is $430, how many of each should they sell in order to maximize profit?

An office company makes desks and drawers. Each desk requires 20 minutes of assembly and 30 minutes of sanding. Each drawer requires 50 minutes of assembly and 7 minutes of sanding. The company has available 3000 minutes for assembly and 2100 minutes for sanding. If the profit per desk is $200 and the profit per drawer is $80, how many of each should the company make to maximize profit?

A milk tea shop owner would like to sell two different milk teas: black milk tea and matcha milk tea. Each contains both milk and honey. A bottle of black milk tea contains 400 grams of milk and 6 grams of honey, whereas a bottle of matcha milk tea contains 570 grams of milk and 4 grams of honey. The profit from each bottle of black milk tea sold is $7.3 and the profit from each bottle of matcha milk tea sold is $4. If his total production must not exceed his available stock of 20000 grams of milk and 600 grams of honey, how many bottles of each type of milk tea should be made to maximize profits?

A young boy is trying to grow taller by drinking milk and eating vegetables. He wants to get a minimum of 90 units of calcium and 60 units of iron per day. A glass of milk costs $1 and contains 30 units of calcium and 18 units of iron. A plate of vegetables costs $3 and contains 8 units of calcium and 20 units of iron. How many of each should he consume to minimize his cost?

Bob wants to design a diet consisting of protein bars and noodles. Assume that each serving of noodles costs $7 and contains 1000 calories and 1.3 grams of protein. Assume that each serving of protein bar costs $1.7 and contains 200 calories and 7 grams of protein. He's interested in spending as little money as possible but he wants to ensure that his meals have at least 3000 calories and at least 32 grams of protein per day. Formulate a linear programming problem that will help minimize the cost of the diet.

A toy store sells plush toys and dolls. Each plush toy costs the store $2 and each doll costs the store $4. The store owner can spend at most $800 on inventory. Each plush toy is then sold for a profit of $3 while each doll is sold for a profit of $4. The owner estimates that at least 80 plush toys but at most 210 plush toys are sold each month. He also estimates that the number of dolls sold is at most twice the amount of plush toys sold. How many of each should be bought and sold to maximize profit?

Forest Paper makes two types of products: graph paper and music paper. Each type of paper requires the use of two machines, a printing machine and a scanning machine. It takes 4 minutes on the printing machine and 4.1 minutes on the scanning machine to make a ream of graph paper. On the other hand, it takes 2.7 minutes on the printing machine and 4 minutes on the scanning machine to make a ream of music paper. Each machine is available for a maximum of 510 minutes per day. The company sells a package of graph paper at a profit of $3 and a package of music paper at a profit of $4.2. The company can sell all the paper it makes. How many reams of each type should the company produce in a day in order to maximize profit? What is that profit?

Calcium and Magnesium are found in two health supplements, health supplement A and health supplement B. One serving of health supplement A contains 60 grams of Calcium and 80 grams of Magnesium. One serving of health supplement B contains 100 grams of Calcium and 20 grams of Magnesium. The cost per health supplement for health supplement A is $11 and the cost per health supplement for health supplement B is $24. A patient must consume these two health supplements every day to get at least 500 grams of Calcium and 80 grams of Magnesium. Determine how much servings of each supplement the patient needs to minimize her daily cost.

Lucy has a dog and she wants his food to be mixed.  In order to keep the dog healthy but also keep the food tasty, the mix needs to have a minimum of 27 units of calcium, 40 units of vitamin mix, and 40 units of protein. A regular brand costs $40 per bag and contains 2 units of calcium, 6 units of vitamin mix, and 7 units of protein. A premium brand costs $23 per bag and contains 10 units of calcium, 7 units of vitamin mix, and 13 units of protein. How many bags of each brand should Lucy mix in order to minimize cost while also meeting the taste and health requirements.

Maple Oil processes three types of crude oil: light oil, non-sticky oil and heavy oil. Each tank of light oil produces a net revenue of $870, each tank of non-sticky oil produces a net revenue of $980, and each tank of heavy oil produces a net revenue of $1800. To process a tank of light oil, 2 units of compound A and 2 units of compound B are required. To process a tank of non-sticky oil, 4 units of compound A and 3 units of compound B are required. To process a tank of heavy oil, 6 units of compound A and 2 units of compound B are required. Currently the company has 130 units of compound A and 100 units of compound B to process. How many full or partial tanks of each oil should the company process so that net revenue is maximized?

A flooring company produces engineered laminate planks and carpets. The chief marketer reports an expected demand of at least 16,000 square feet of laminate planks and 6,000 square feet of carpets each week. The shipping contract requires a total of at least 30,000 square feet of products each week. However, due to a shortage of raw materials, no more than 20,000 square feet of laminate planks and 10,000 square feet of carpets can be produced weekly. If a square foot of laminate planks produces a $1.9 profit and a square foot of carpets yields a $4.3 profit, how many of each type of product should be made weekly to maximize the company's profit?

A man takes two supplements to get his daily iron and calcium requirements. A pill of supplement A has 4 units of iron and 7 units of calcium. A pill of supplement B contains 6 units of iron and 9 units of calcium.  The man needs a minimum of 30 units of iron and 70 units of calcium per day. If the cost per pill of supplement A is $3 and the cost per pill of supplement B is  $5, how many of each should he buy to minimize costs?

A fashion company sells regular handbags and premium handbags made of higher quality material. They can sell regular handbags at a profit of $40 each and premium handbags at a profit of $110 each. The total monthly cost of manufacturing is $300 per regular handbag and $689 per premium handbag. The company has a total budget of $390000 and can sell at most 248 handbags of either type per month. How many of each handbag should they sell to maximize its monthly profit?

A repairman fixes washing machines and freezers. Each washing machine takes 20 minutes of inspection and 100 minutes of fixing time. Each freezer takes 30 minutes of inspection and 110 minutes of fixing time. The repairman has 8000 minutes available for inspection and 40000 minutes available in his schedule. If each washing machine repaired earns him $490 and each freezer repaired earns his $222, how many of each appliance should he fix to maximize his earnings?

Super Shop sells cat paw snacks and gold shark snacks in bulk. It plans to sell them into two snack mix products. The first mix contains 30% cat paw snacks and 50% gold shark snacks. The second mix contains 24% cat paw snacks and 36% gold shark snacks. The store has on hand 30 kg of cat paw snacks and 70 kg of gold shark snacks. If the profit per kg of the first mix is $13 and the profit per kg of the second mix is $16, how many kg of each should be prepared to maximize profit?

A taco stand sells regular tacos and deluxe tacos with extra meat. The stand makes x1 regular tacos at a profit of $1.90 each and x2 deluxe tacos at a profit of $2.50 each (x1 and x2 are unknown variables both greater than or equal to 0). There is a demand for at most 40 regular tacos and at most 30 deluxe tacos. The stand only has enough supplies to sell at most 50 tacos of either type. How many of each taco should the stand make to maximize profit?

A printing company sells math workbooks and English workbooks. To meet demand, they must make at least 60 math workbooks and at least 80 English workbooks. However, they can make at most 230 math workbooks and at most 290 English workbooks. The company has a contract with a school to send at least 300 workbooks of either type. If the profit per math workbook is $12 and the profit per English workbook is $15, how many of each should the company make to maximize profit?

A music company produces two types of digital keyboards, one is full-weighted and another is semi-weighted. Both keyboards are sold for $1900 and $4400 respectively. There are about 6400 oscillator chips available every day from which the full-weighted version requires 40 chips while the semi-weighted version requires 26 chips. The company has a total of 4 working hours a day. Both of these keyboards require a production time of 2.2 hours. What should be the manufacturing quantity for each of the keyboards to maximize the total revenue?

Platinum Database sells two types of subscription software packages: a personal license and a commercial license which will cost $330 and $3000 to generate respectively. The marketing department estimates that they can sell at most 600 licenses for both versions combined a month. The profit per personal license is $340 and the profit per commercial version is $1000. If the company does not want to spend more than $700000, how many of each software package should they produce to maximize the profits.

Zeta Bakery sells two types of cookies. They sell a strawberry cookie and a sugar cookie. Let's say they make x1 strawberry cookies, at a profit of $5.1 each, and x2 sugar cookies, at a profit of $8 each (x1 and x2 are unknowns both greater than or equal to 0). The daily demand for these cookies is at most 60 strawberry cookies and at most 90 sugar cookies. The bakery is short staffed and can make a maximum of 60 cookies of either type per day. How much of each cookie should the bakery make in order to maximize profit?

document: A food company would like to run its commercials on three streaming platforms: Pi TV, Beta Video and Gamma Live. The cost for a commercial as well as the expected audience reach is given. On Pi TV, a commercial costs $1300 and attracts 3000 viewers. On Beta Video, a commercial costs $3000 and attracts 4000 viewers. On Gamma Live, a commercial costs $6000 and attracts 8000 viewers.
